TLT.text: \caption{\textbf{Two Core Limitations.} (a) Semantic transition types (forward, skip, epsilon, backward). (b) Lack explicit guidance, causing flattening in standard GNNs. (c) Static global embeddings ignore multi-scale temporal structure, leading to myopia. HiLTL addresses both via SE-GNN semantics and hierarchical value.}

\caption{Complete HiLTL System. Four components: (1) LTL-to-LDBA product generating $q_t$ and observations; (2) SE-GNN with edge-conditioned attention over semantic features; (3) Dual-pathway value with multi-scale short-term and automaton-driven long-term; (4) Dynamic fusion via $\beta(q)$ producing final Q-values.}

\caption{Fusion overview: The diagram illustrates the dual-pathway value decomposition strategy: \textbf{(1) Short-term pathway} (top) uses Multi-Scale SE-GNN to extract hierarchical embeddings from three GATv2 layers, capturing immediate sub-goals (Layer 1), mid-term planning (Layer 2), and global structure (Layer 3); \textbf{(2) Long-term pathway} (bottom) leverages Automaton Tracking to compute acceptance proximity and transition history. The dynamic fusion weight $\beta(q)$ (Eq.~\ref{eq:beta_definition}) adaptively balances both pathways based on distance to acceptance states. Final V-value: $V(s,q) = (1-\beta(q)) V_{\text{short}} + \beta(q) V_{\text{long}}$.}

\caption{LDBA with HiLTL Enhancements for Formula $(\neg \text{blue} \mathrel{U} \text{green}) \land F \text{yellow}$. The automaton structure shows how our three core innovations are integrated: \textbf{(1) SE-GNN Enhancement} adds 6-dimensional edge features (transition types: forward/skip/epsilon/trap, semantic distance) and 4-dimensional node features (accepting status, SCC membership, distance to acceptance); \textbf{(2) Multi-Scale GNN} extracts hierarchical embeddings through 3 layers (Layer 0: local 1-hop neighborhoods for short-term decisions, Layer 1: 2-hop mid-range patterns, Layer 2: global topology for long-term planning); \textbf{(3) Hierarchical Value} computes $V_{\text{short}}(s)$ from environment state and $V_{\text{long}}(q)$ from automaton state, with dynamic fusion weight $\beta(q)$ that increases as the agent approaches accepting states. Edge categories distinguish transition types: forward chains (solid), skip edges (dashed), self-loops (solid), and trap transitions (dash-dot). The accepting state $q_{acc}$ forms an SCC, while trap state $q_{trap}$ represents formula violation.}

\caption{ZoneEnv visualization examples under two typical LTL objectives, shown as two rows spanning both columns. Top: $G\,F$ blue $\wedge\, G\,F$ yellow-repeatedly visit blue and yellow regions, exhibiting back-and-forth movements across mixed color blocks. Bottom: $F\,G$ green-reach the green region and maintain residence, stabilizing near the specified area.}

\caption{Performance Improvement Analysis Across Configurations and Task Difficulties. \textbf{Left:} success-rate gains of representative variants over baseline, with hv\_only at +4.5\%, msgnn\_only at +2.3\%, and hv\_track at +6.4\% (strongest on hard tasks). \textbf{Right:} improvements grouped by LDBA size: easy tasks (0--10 states) gain 1.2\%, medium tasks (11--15) gain 2.9\%, and hard tasks (16+) retain +4.3\% for hv\_track.}
